_doc:
The FIRST scenario that drives `generic_v1` to a completed deliverable. Four scenarios already name project type `generic` and NONE produces a master: `happy_path` pauses after brief_intake (it is the pause/cancel probe and is correct as-is), `multi_source_happy_path` pauses after source_ingest, and `panel_image_happy_path` / `storyboard_merge` use a throwaway generic project only to reach an API. So the generic blueprint — the default content type — has never been proven to render anything in E2E. This scenario closes that hole and nothing else.

Shape: the project/brief/voice block is copied VERBATIM from `happy_path.json`, because that block is the one already proven to thread through brief_intake (its five `equals` checks are the proof). Exactly two things change, and only the two that are required to reach a deliverable:
  (1) `run.pause_after_stages: []` — explicit empty list = AUTOPILOT (src/api/schemas/runs.py:174-182). This is REQUIRED, not cosmetic: the generic blueprint declares `default_pause_after=True` on script_draft and storyboard_draft (src/services/blueprints/generic.py:32,39) and `default_pause_after_stages` seeds from those specs when the field is omitted (src/services/run_engine.py:140), so an omitted field would pause this run twice and never render. `promo_happy_path` carries the same explicit `[]` for the same reason.
  (2) `expect_terminal_status: ["completed"]`.

Stages exercised end to end: brief_intake -> script_draft (LLM) -> storyboard_draft (LLM) -> narrate (TTS) -> video_render (video-compiler). ai_image_gen, ai_video_gen, motion_graphics_gen, source_ingest and media_discovery are all OPT-IN and skip clean without their config block (ai_image_gen.py:108-113), so this is the plain generic path with no GPU / image-backend / KAG dependency. That is deliberate: the first proof of a content type should fail for product reasons, not because mini1 was busy.

DEADLINE: 3600s / timeout_minutes 70, the same pair `promo_happy_path` carries. Based on structural equivalence, NOT on a measurement — there is no measurement to base it on, because this blueprint has never completed a run in E2E. promo_v1 is the closest completing sibling: LLM script + LLM storyboard + TTS narrate + a single video-compiler master, the same five-stage shape and the same downstream services. It is deliberately generous rather than tight: a deadline below real runtime produces a FALSE RED, and this repo has been burned by exactly that (a promo reported failed at a 1200s budget that really took 1386s; app_review and course each produced the same false red twice in September). 3600 also stays under `pipeline.run_deadline_seconds` (7200), as tests/test_e2e_scenario_contracts.py::test_no_scenario_waits_longer_than_the_run_itself_may_live requires. RE-MEASURE this from the `runs` table after the first handful of green completions and size it the way the promo/course entries are sized (measured max x ~1.25), rather than leaving a structurally-guessed number in place forever.

⚠️ The deadline is NOT a key in this file — the harness takes it from `--deadline-seconds` (scripts/e2e_validate.py:3324) and the matrix supplies it per scenario. This scenario therefore needs an entry in `scripts/e2e_scenarios/matrix.json` before anything runs it; that file was owned by another lane when this was written and is deliberately untouched here.
_ordered_duration_doc:
generic DOES read an ordered duration, and it reads it from the BRIEF, not from the deliverable. The chain is: `brief.target_duration_seconds` -> `src/services/stages/generic/brief_intake.py:47` (`int(brief.get("target_duration_seconds", 60))`) -> `src/services/stages/generic/script_draft.py:106`, which writes it into the script prompt as "Write a script for a {n}-second video". That is the ONLY resolver: the generic blueprint has no reconcile_timeline stage and no `direction.timing.target_seconds` override, and nothing downstream of script_draft imposes a duration ceiling — a generic film is exactly as long as its narration.

So the order is set ONCE, in `brief.target_duration_seconds: 30`, matching happy_path's proven value. A deliverable-level `target_duration_seconds` is deliberately NOT set: no generic stage reads one, so adding it would be a number that steers nothing while making `_ordered_seconds` in the contract tests believe it is authoritative. Fabricating an order is the bug this branch removes.

brief.audience: solo founders filing their own accounts

_assert_doc:
Two stage assertions, both copied in spelling from proven siblings.

brief_intake: the five `equals` checks are lifted UNCHANGED from happy_path.json, including its 2026-09-05 strengthening — angle/audience/voice_descriptor are set to values no default can produce (brief_intake defaults them to 'informational'/'general'/'neutral'), so they fail closed if the brief or the voice block is dropped from config_snapshot rather than passing vacuously. They are free here and they localise a threading failure to the first stage instead of to a blank film.

video_render: `nonempty artifact_url` only — the same spelling `lesson_motion_slides_happy_path.json` uses on lesson_compile and `promo_happy_path.json` uses on promo_render. There is deliberately NO `numeric_gte duration_seconds` floor, unlike promo. A sized floor requires a measured minimum (tests/test_e2e_scenario_contracts.py `_MEASURED_FLOOR_MINIMA`, `_FLOOR_SAFETY = 2.0`) and this blueprint has produced ZERO completed E2E runs, so any number here would be invented, not sized — which is the exact defect that guard exists to catch. Add one once there are completions to measure, and record it in `_MEASURED_FLOOR_MINIMA` with its sample size in the same change.
_pixel_doc:
Media ACCEPTANCE probes on the delivered master (scripts/e2e_validate.py _MEDIA_CHECKS), spelled exactly as promo_happy_path.json and lesson_motion_slides_happy_path.json spell them. `artifact_reachable` proves the object downloads and DECODES (a non-blank url string proves neither); `audio_present` proves an audio stream exists AND is not digital silence (ffmpeg volumedetect mean/peak dBFS) — the single check most likely to catch a generic render that composited pictures over nothing; `resolution` reads the ENCODED width/height rather than the number the stage reports about itself; `stream_durations` measures the VIDEO and AUDIO stream durations SEPARATELY and never the container, because a container duration is the MAX over its streams and can never refute a truncated video track.

The stream_durations minima (3s video / 2s audio) are EMPTY-RENDER floors, not sized floors, and they are stated as such: this blueprint has no measured distribution yet. They are set far below anything a 30s order could plausibly yield so that they fail only on a stub or a one-frame render, and they must be re-derived from measured runs before anyone treats them as a quality gate.

`duration_within_tolerance` is present but DISARMED (`"enabled": false`), matching every sibling except action_reel_happy_path.json — the ONE calibrated exemption — and the guard tests/scripts/test_e2e_media_probes.py::test_only_the_calibrated_scenario_arms_the_duration_tolerance_check. `ordered_seconds: 30` records the order the brief actually places (see _ordered_duration_doc). Arming it is out of scope here — duration calibration is in flight fleet-wide and a red instrument on known-in-flight work teaches people to ignore the instrument.

expect_pixel_checks._doc: Header-vs-packets guard on the delivered master. THE incident: an mp4 whose `moov` declared 12.0s over data that demuxed to 2.84s of picture. Every header-reading duration assertion reads that same claim -- in the recorded case `stream_durations` even saw a 0.00s A/V skew, because both numbers came from the one lying mux -- so a master whose picture stopped 9s early passed all of them. This is the only check that compares the DECLARED duration against the duration that actually demuxes (packet count / avg_frame_rate), which is what makes the disagreement visible. No thresholds are pinned here on purpose: the tolerance lives once, in scripts/e2e_validate.py.
